title: Predictive modelling of laser-driven control of real materials

concept.text: Discovered Materials grand challenge 04 (Tuning Materials with Light): model what a laser pulse does to a real material, treating electrons and lattice vibrations together over long timescales in a tractable way. Sources given: https://discoveredmaterials.com/grand-challenges/.

change_log.change: Added by hand to MAS on 2026-11-15.
change_log.reason: Grand challenge published by Discovered Materials (Matforge Inc.), open as of November 2026 with a USD 1 million prize pool; added at the owner's request, November 14, 2026.

page.title: Predictive theory of light-driven materials
page.definition: A computational method predicts how light drives a material’s electrons and phonons, the quantized vibrations of its atomic lattice, through excitation and relaxation. It treats electron–electron, electron–phonon and phonon–phonon interactions together and reproduces specified model and material benchmarks.

goal.need: Full two-time nonequilibrium Green-function propagation has runtime proportional to Nₜ³, where Nₜ counts time steps. Graphite measurements span the pulse duration and post-excitation delay shown below, requiring predictions of energy transfer from electrons into lattice vibrations and redistribution among vibration modes.

completion.title: Discovered Materials accepts one method as solving its Tuning Materials with Light challenge.
completion.criterion: Discovered Materials determines that a reproducible method meets every success criterion of Challenge 04, including the Hubbard model and three material reproductions in m1–m4. The challenge seeks simultaneous electron–electron, electron–phonon and phonon–phonon interactions and orders-of-magnitude acceleration over pure nonequilibrium Green-function calculations. Judging also considers predictive agreement, computational effort, and recovery of weak-drive and equilibrium limits. Numerical error tolerances and a minimum speedup are unspecified.
completion.set_by: Matforge, Inc., doing business as Discovered Materials; Grand Challenges Official Rules, Sections 4–5, incorporating the Challenge 04 technical description.
completion.threshold_quote: A challenge is "solved" only when a submission meets every success criterion in its Challenge Description, as determined by Sponsor under Section 5.
completion.basis: The rules require every criterion to be satisfied under sponsor assessment. The milestones are parallel component tests; completion requires their joint satisfaction and the sponsor’s evaluation of the method. Challenge 04 remained marked open on 14 November 2026.

milestones.title: A method reproduces the 11-site Hubbard chain through tJ/ħ = 50 and the ladder benchmarks.
milestones.criterion: Reproduce Schroedter et al., Figures 2–3: density imbalance and correlated double occupancy in an 11-site Hubbard chain at U/J = 5 and 15 through tJ/ħ = 50, plus U/J = 0–20. Reproduce Figures 8–9: equilibrium and laser-driven spin correlations of a 6×2 ladder; and Figure 10: optical-conductivity thresholds and line shapes at U/J = 3, 6 and 12, against the specified converged or exact references. U is interaction energy, J hopping energy and ħ the reduced Planck constant. The preprint submitted on 9 June 2026 reports approximate-method comparisons; it is not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: Discovered Materials, Challenge 04; electronic-correlations reproduction target.

milestones.title: A method reproduces WSe₂ dark-exciton formation in about 400 fs.
milestones.criterion: Reproduce Madéo et al., Figures 2–4: energy- and momentum-resolved photoemission and complete bright/dark exciton population traces in monolayer WSe₂ at 90 K under resonant 1.72 eV and above-gap 2.48 eV excitation. Include approximately 400 fs dark-exciton buildup and a late-time bright/dark population ratio near 0.5 under resonant excitation. Excitons are bound electron–hole pairs; these dark states require momentum transfer to couple to light. The experiment was published on 4 December 2020; an erratum was published on 22 May 2025.
milestones.set_by: Discovered Materials, Challenge 04; WSe₂ reproduction target.

milestones.title: A method reproduces graphite’s resolved phonon populations from 0.5 to 100 ps.
milestones.criterion: Reproduce René de Cotret et al., Figures 2 and 6–7: graphite diffuse-scattering maps and optical and acoustic phonon populations at 0.5, 1.5, 5 and 100 ps after 35 fs, 800 nm, 12 mJ/cm² excitation. Include growth and decay of the K-point A₁′ optical mode and energy transfer into acoustic branches. Their experiment, published on 19 December 2019, extracted mode populations and an A₁′-projected electron–phonon coupling strength of 0.035 ± 0.001 eV².
milestones.set_by: Discovered Materials, Challenge 04; graphite reproduction target.

milestones.title: A method reproduces MgB₂’s nonlinear response and conductivity 2 ps after a 150 kV/cm pump.
milestones.criterion: Reproduce Katsumi et al., Figures 2–4 and Supplemental Figure S3: the MgB₂ film’s superconducting transition at 38 K, lower-gap temperature curve, nonlinear peak near 1 THz at 7 K, and first- and third-harmonic responses under 0.63 THz driving across temperature and field. Include the monotonic normalized first-harmonic increase on cooling and complex conductivity at 2 ps after a 150 kV/cm pump. The experiment, published on 16 July 2025, measured condensate depletion under the strong pump.
milestones.set_by: Discovered Materials, Challenge 04; MgB₂ reproduction target.

not_found: No numerical acceptance tolerances, minimum speedup or prescribed computing hardware were found in Challenge 04 or its official rules.
No published submission satisfying all four reproduction targets with one method was found.
The full text of the WSe₂ paper’s erratum of 22 May 2025 could not be opened, leaving its effect on the benchmark unchecked.

results.finding: A simulation of monolayer WSe₂ (sample size not stated) reports an approximately 180 fs intervalley exciton transfer timescale.
results.detail: The simulated photoemission intensities and late-time valley ratio agree with the experiment in overall behavior. However, the simulation uses 100 K and a 1.85 eV resonant pump; it does not demonstrate the specified 90 K, 1.72 eV and 2.48 eV benchmark or approximately 400 fs buildup.
